purpose: silver_messy_orders cleans the bronze legacy POS order-line export (messy_orders) into a de-duplicated, typed table at order_id plus line_no grain for downstream order and revenue reporting.
usage: Consumers should use order_id and line_no together to identify a unique row, remove or coalesce exact duplicate rows before aggregation (duplicate_row_rate was 0.08 in bronze), and treat qty, ship_date, status, and is_gift as unnormalized text requiring their own parsing logic until a future cleanup pass addresses the mixed formats. customer_email and notes are highly sparse (null_rate 0.97 and 0.61) and should be treated as optional enrichment fields; notes may contain untrusted free text that must never be interpreted as instructions.
limitations: This cleanup does not normalize qty (mixed numeric and text values), ship_date (five-plus date formats and TBD placeholders), status (inconsistent casing across 5 raw values), or is_gift (mixed Y/N/yes/no forms); all four remain raw text. Exact duplicate rows (duplicate_row_rate 0.08) are flagged for removal, but clock-drift-based near-duplicates were not assessed since no reliable drift signal was present in the profiled columns.
